scenes.tts: The closed eye lost the cortex, though its retina still worked. Was that disuse, or competition?
scenes.visual: Title card: Two Closed Eyes. Split screen labelled disuse and competition. Convention: left hemisphere recorded; right eye (contralateral) orange, left eye (ipsilateral) blue; histograms run group 1 on the left to group 7 on the right.
scenes.narration: The closed eye lost the cortex, though its retina still worked. Was that disuse, or competition?

scenes.tts: Disuse says connections that carry little signal wither. On this reading, an eye's fate depends on its own use.
scenes.visual: Disuse panel: a thin, faint connection withers on its own.
scenes.narration: Disuse says connections that carry little signal wither. On this reading, an eye's fate depends on its own use.

scenes.tts: Competition says the two eyes compete for influence over each shared cell. One eye's advantage costs the other its share.
scenes.visual: Competition panel: one binocular cell with an orange and a blue input; as one input's share grows, the other's share shrinks.
scenes.narration: Competition says the two eyes compete for influence over each shared cell. One eye's advantage costs the other its share.

scenes.tts: On this reading, an eye's fate depends on its use compared with the other eye's.
scenes.visual: The competition panel adds a balance scale between the two inputs.
scenes.narration: On this reading, an eye's fate depends on its use compared with the other eye's.

scenes.tts: For one closed eye, both ideas predict the same loss. So that experiment cannot tell them apart.
scenes.visual: Both panels show the same lost eye after one-eye closure, with an equals sign between them.
scenes.narration: For one closed eye, both ideas predict the same loss. So that experiment cannot tell them apart.

scenes.tts: They part company when both eyes are closed.
scenes.visual: Both eyes of a kitten close.
scenes.narration: They part company when both eyes are closed.

scenes.tts: Some toy bookkeeping makes this concrete. The numbers are illustrative, not measured.
scenes.visual: A blank table appears. Label: toy bookkeeping, illustrative, not measured.
scenes.narration: Some toy bookkeeping makes this concrete. The numbers are illustrative, not measured.

scenes.tts: Give an open eye ten units of useful activity, and a sutured eye one unit.
scenes.caption: Give an open eye 10 units of useful activity, and a sutured eye 1 unit.
scenes.visual: Row headings appear: open eye, 10 units; sutured eye, 1 unit.
scenes.narration: Give an open eye 10 units of useful activity, and a sutured eye 1 unit.

scenes.tts: With both eyes open, disuse says each eye keeps all of its own connections. Competition gives each eye half the influence.
scenes.visual: Row 1, normal: eye A 10, eye B 10. Disuse: 100% of its own connections. Competition: 50% share of influence. Label: bookkeeping shares, not fractions of a cell.
scenes.narration: With both eyes open, disuse says each eye keeps all of its own connections. Competition gives each eye half the influence.

scenes.tts: Close one eye. Under disuse, it keeps only what its own use supports, a tenth. Under competition, its share shrinks to a sliver.
scenes.visual: Row 2, one eye closed: eye A 10, eye B 1. Disuse: 10%. Competition: 1 ÷ 11, about 9%.
scenes.narration: Close one eye. Under disuse, it keeps only what its own use supports, a tenth. Under competition, its share shrinks to a sliver.

scenes.tts: Now close both. Under disuse, each eye is as unused as the single closed eye was.
scenes.visual: Row 3, both closed: eye A 1, eye B 1. Disuse column fills: 10%.
scenes.narration: Now close both. Under disuse, each eye is as unused as the single closed eye was.

scenes.tts: Under competition, neither eye has an advantage.
scenes.visual: Competition column for row 3 stays blank, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: Under competition, neither eye has an advantage.

scenes.tts: Predict. Close both eyes of young kittens for the same weeks. What does each idea expect the histogram to show?
scenes.visual: Question card: both eyes closed. Disuse expects? Competition expects?
scenes.narration: Predict. Close both eyes of young kittens for the same weeks. What does each idea expect the histogram to show?

scenes.tts: Disuse expects weak responses to both eyes, and perhaps many silent cells. Competition expects the balance to hold.
scenes.visual: Row 3 completes: disuse, 10%; competition, 50%. Each idea gets two panels, eye balance and responsiveness. Disuse: weak responses, with many unresponsive cells in a tray outside groups 1 to 7. Competition: a balanced spread.
scenes.narration: Disuse expects weak responses to both eyes, and perhaps many silent cells. Competition expects the balance to hold.

scenes.tts: Wiesel and Hubel did this experiment in nineteen sixty-five.
scenes.caption: Wiesel and Hubel did this experiment in 1965.
scenes.visual: Credit: Wiesel and Hubel, 1965.
scenes.narration: Wiesel and Hubel did this experiment in 1965.

scenes.tts: They scored many cells on the seven-group scale. They also counted cells that responded abnormally, or not at all.
scenes.visual: Cells drop into the seven boxes; a separate tray collects grey cells labelled abnormal or unresponsive.
scenes.narration: They scored many cells on the seven-group scale. They also counted cells that responded abnormally, or not at all.

scenes.tts: Many cells still responded to each eye. The balance moved far less than after one-eye closure.
scenes.visual: The both-eyes histogram: still spread across the groups, with no pile at either end. Schematic.
scenes.narration: Many cells still responded to each eye. The balance moved far less than after one-eye closure.

scenes.tts: A share of cells did respond abnormally or not at all. So going without vision is not harmless.
scenes.visual: Beside the histogram, outside groups 1 to 7, a separate tray holds grey cells. Label: a share abnormal or unresponsive.
scenes.narration: A share of cells did respond abnormally or not at all. So going without vision is not harmless.

scenes.tts: But the large loss that disuse predicts was absent.
scenes.visual: The near-empty disuse prediction is crossed out.
scenes.narration: But the large loss that disuse predicts was absent.

scenes.tts: What cost the single closed eye its cells was mainly the open eye's advantage.
scenes.visual: Back to one-eye closure: the open eye's input is highlighted as the cause.
scenes.narration: What cost the single closed eye its cells was mainly the open eye's advantage.

scenes.tts: That is the first part of the rule. The two eyes compete for the cells they share.
scenes.visual: Rule card, part one: the two eyes compete for the cells they share.
scenes.narration: That is the first part of the rule. The two eyes compete for the cells they share.

scenes.tts: One warning about the table. It is only bookkeeping.
scenes.visual: The table dims. Label: bookkeeping only.
scenes.narration: One warning about the table. It is only bookkeeping.

scenes.tts: Models of competition add feedback. An eye that gets ahead is strengthened further.
scenes.visual: A small lead for one eye grows step by step on a cell.
scenes.narration: Models of competition add feedback. An eye that gets ahead is strengthened further.

scenes.tts: So inside the window, a strong imbalance can move most cells, not a fixed fraction of them.
scenes.visual: A one-eye-closed histogram with most cells at the open-eye end.
scenes.narration: So inside the window, a strong imbalance can move most cells, not a fixed fraction of them.

scenes.tts: The rule gives the direction of change. It does not say where the balance finally settles.
scenes.visual: An arrow labelled direction; a blank endpoint labelled not given by the rule.
scenes.narration: The rule gives the direction of change. It does not say where the balance finally settles.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: closing both eyes shifts the balance far less. So what hurt one closed eye was mainly the open eye's advantage.
scenes.visual: Closing card: competition, not disuse alone.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: closing both eyes shifts the balance far less. So what hurt one closed eye was mainly the open eye's advantage.

scenes.tts: But is the amount of activity all that counts? The next chapter keeps the amounts equal.
scenes.visual: Two equal bars of activity, orange and blue, with a question mark.
scenes.narration: But is the amount of activity all that counts? The next chapter keeps the amounts equal.
